column183: 09x01 - The New Guys;Pete: I don't want it, really.
column184: 09x01 - The New Guys;Angela: How would you support the cat? What are your ambitions?
column185: 09x01 - The New Guys;Pete: I want to start my own business. I want to be a millionaire. Lots of things. Travel, make the world a better place, earn an MBA at night.
column186: 09x01 - The New Guys;Angela: Have you taken any concrete steps?
column187: 09x01 - The New Guys;Pete: Well, I'm still just fitting in here, you know? Getting used to the new job. But, definitely on the agenda. But that is a good idea, Angela. I should make a list.
column188: 09x01 - The New Guys;Jim: Oh, come on, Pete! God, that's just sad. If he doesn't watch himself, he's gonna be here for years, doing nothing. [sober realization] Wow, maybe Pete is the new Jim.
column189: 09x01 - The New Guys;Dwight: Do you see how the trapeze completely surrounds the wire? That means it's literally impossible for anyone to fall off. So you will merely sit below and be my counterweight as I pedal across the parking lot to that telephone pole.
column190: 09x01 - The New Guys;Pam: I will?
column191: 09x01 - The New Guys;Dwight: You will. Yeah we weigh about the same, wouldn't you say?
column192: 09x01 - The New Guys;Pam: Sure, if you weigh 105 pounds.
column193: 09x01 - The New Guys;Dwight: So you'll do it?
column194: 09x01 - The New Guys;Pam: No.
column195: 09x01 - The New Guys;Dwight: Come on, this will be the only thrill of your boring life.
column196: 09x01 - The New Guys;Pam: Dwight, you may find this hard to believe, but I love my boring life.
column197: 09x01 - The New Guys;Dwight: Come on.
column198: 09x01 - The New Guys;Pam: Exactly the way it is.
column199: 09x01 - The New Guys;Dwight: No, Pam.
column200: 09x01 - The New Guys;Pam: Yes, and there's nothing you could say that would get me to run the slightest risk of losing it.
column201: 09x01 - The New Guys;Dwight: Please? Please, Pam?
column202: 09x01 - The New Guys;Pam: Find someone else, I don't know. Ask Phyllis.

column206: 09x01 - The New Guys;Pete: Your husband?
column207: 09x01 - The New Guys;Angela: No, the baby. Please, it's my husband's favorite cat. He's broken up about it. It's the only time I've seen him cry other than our wedding night.
column208: 09x01 - The New Guys;Oscar: You know what? I will take Comstock.
column209: 09x01 - The New Guys;Angela: Really? Oh, Oscar, thank you!
column210: 09x01 - The New Guys;Oscar: I'll come by after work and pick him up.
column211: 09x01 - The New Guys;Angela: Yay! Oh, poor Robert. He won't get to say goodbye. He has this business dinner tonight
column212: 09x01 - The New Guys;Oscar: C'est la vie.
column213: 09x01 - The New Guys;Angela: Please don't teach the cat French.
column214: 09x01 - The New Guys;Oscar: [on phone] Yeah. Good news, tonight when you come over for dinner, you can play with your old buddy Comstock.
column215: 09x01 - The New Guys;Pam: You ready?

column217: 09x01 - The New Guys;Pam: Kay.
column218: 09x01 - The New Guys;Dwight: Ok. [prepares bike trapeze]Oh, god.
column219: 09x01 - The New Guys;[Jim tries dialing and hangs up]
column220: 09x01 - The New Guys;Dwight: Attention, employees of Dunder Mifflin. Everyone thinks the new guys are so cool cause they can slack line. Boo. Hey Clark, this is what a areal salesman looks like. They say that you only live once and I'm about to prove it. Dwight Schrute!
column221: 09x01 - The New Guys;Jim: Hey, man. It's halpert. Did you go to the other guy yet? Great, don't. I'm in. Yeah, yep, I'm all in. Ok, talk to you soon. Bye. [hangs up] Yeah!
column222: 09x01 - The New Guys;Dwight: Woo! [starts pedaling out until trapeze bike flips over, he dangles from the handlebars] Ahh!!

column224: 09x01 - The New Guys;Meredith: Crap. Sorry, Nellie.
column225: 09x01 - The New Guys;Nellie: Once again, I understand that old habits die hard, but if everyone would kindly walk their refuse to the trash bins instead of tossing them, then we would—[hit in the face with trash]
column226: 09x01 - The New Guys;Stanley: Mm, swish.
column227: 09x01 - The New Guys;Nellie: Oh, it's nothing to do with me. I just happen to be sitting near to where the bins are.
column228: 09x01 - The New Guys;Andy: There are two things that I am passionate about. Recycling and revenge.
column229: 09x01 - The New Guys;Nellie: [As trash is thrown at her] Fluke.

column1: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: [surveying an untidy office] The building's custodian is on vacation for the month and Dwight is too cheap to hire a replacement. So, instead, we're living in filth. But, not for long. Because I have created the chore wheel.
column2: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Kevin: [viewing the chore wheel for the first time] Oh, yeah! Can I spin first?
column3: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: Well, it doesn't spin. We'll just move the wheel one notch each morning and... you see what chore you get that day.
column4: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Kevin: A wheel is supposed to spin.
column5: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Erin: Yeah, you know, like [motions arm in circles] guh, guh, guh, guh, guh, guh, guh... guh.
column6: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: No, I'm familiar with spinning. It's just that wouldn't work with a chore wheel because people might get the same chore-
column7: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Andy: [interrupting] Bugh, boring. All she talks about is chores.
column8: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Creed: A wheel wants to spin, Pam.
column9: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: [reluctantly] Spinning would be more fun.
column10: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: [frustrated] ‘Kay.
column11: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Kevin: [spinning a new ‘chore wheel' while everyone claps] Okay, that's what I'm talking about! Big money, big money! [wheel stops on ‘mug duty', disappointed] Mug duty?
column12: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: Yes, you clean all the mugs in the sink.
column13: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Kevin: This sucks.
column14: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Erin: Yeah, seriously, it's like everything on there is work.
column15: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: I don't think you guys understand why we're doing this. It's-
column16: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Kevin: Yeah, I don't think that you understand wheels.
column17: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: I've been through several rounds of development with the team and here's where we stand with the chore wheel. [introducing a third ‘chore wheel', excited] We've got prizes! Ten bucks, candy bar, manager for an hour but, there are also penalties. Like, no internet, Stanley gets your lunch. The one thing that is not on the chore wheel is chores. But they were right; it's more fun this way.
column18: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: [everyone cheers as Meredith spins and lands on ‘tiny wheel'] The tiny wheel actually does have chores. It's so cute no one seems to mind.
column19: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: [referencing the ‘tiny wheel'] Toilets! [everyone cheers as Meredith accepts her chore]
column20: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: [at the Halpert residence as Cece twirls in the front yard, exiting front door] Pam, we gotta go. Cece, go back inside. Grandma's got breakfast, OK? [to camera] We are going to Roy's wedding. Yep, Roy. I think the only weird thing about going to your wife's ex-fiancé's wedding on a weekday at eight AM is that it's your wife's ex-fiancé.
column21: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: [exiting house] Thanks, mom!
column22: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: [to Pam] A banana?
column23: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: Yeah. I'm afraid he's only gonna have hot dogs.
column24: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: Oh, come on. Not even Roy will have hot dogs at his wedding.
column25: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: Planned a wedding with him. He wanted hot dogs.
column26: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: [to camera] Just... so weird.
column27: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Erin: [as Pete and Clark enter office] Oh, Pete, you've got mail.
column28: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pete: Really? I got something?
column29: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Erin: Well, it's addressed to Customer Service so, it's your mail.
column30: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Clark: Well, you know, I'm also Customer Service.
column31: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Erin: Yeah, I'm alternating. [gestures both men]
column32: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pete: [sarcastically] Yay, another person yelling at me.
column33: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Erin: Well, it could be a nice letter. I write nice letters to companies all the time.
column34: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pete: That's really nice.
column35: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Clark: [looking down at Erin's desk] Wow, Newsweek, huh? This election... thing is crazy, right?
column36: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pete: [referring to the letter] It's open.
column37: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Erin: Oh yeah, I accidentally read it. It's not a nice letter.
column38: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pete: [whispering] OK.
column39: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: [distributing paperwork to the office] Get excited. The special projects fairy has arrived.
column40: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Creed: I know you don't really exist.
column41: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: Today, I launch my big charity initiative ‘Operation Give Back'. Andy has shot down all of my special projects thus far but, this one is about charity. So, I'd like to see him piss on that one.
column42: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Roy: [at Roy's wedding] Darryl! Ha-ha! What's happening?
column43: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Darryl: Congratulations, baby!
column44: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Roy: Ah, thank you!
column45: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: [Jim and Pam approaching the wedding venue] Is this his house?
column46: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: Think so.
column47: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Server: [approaching Jim and Pam] Mimosa?
column48: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: [taking glass] Thank you.
column49: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Server: Would you like me to take your peel?
column50: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: [embarrassed] Yes, thank you. [finishes banana and hands server the peel]
column51: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: OK.
column52: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: [as Jim receives and declines a call] Who's that?
column53: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: Uh, my ex-fiancé.
column54: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: [sarcastically] Ha-ha.
column55: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: I started a new business with my college friend. But, Pam doesn't know. Um... actually I did tell Pam and we decided ‘no'. But, then I decided 'yes' anyway. So, I'm thinking there's another conversation coming. And, it's hard to know when that will be.
column56: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: With Operation Give Back, you pick the charities Dunder-Mifflin supports.
column57: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Kevin: [grinning] Oh boy! What's happening?
column58: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: There's four thousand dollars to give away. So, who has filled out their form? Stanley?
column59: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Stanley: American Diabetes Association.
column60: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Angela: Um, you have diabetes, Stanley. [to Nellie] I'm sorry, is the assignment to pick a selfish charity?
column61: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Toby: I w-, uh, I would love to give uh-
column62: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Kevin: [excited] Heifer's International. Listen to this. They give a poor person like, a goat or something. It's a great prank.
column63: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Creed: I wanna work with, uh, Jimmy Carter and help build gnomes.
column64: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: Dwight, what about you?
column65: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Dwight: I will not be participating as there is no evidence that charity works.
column66: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Andy: Uh, correction, I give to a foundation that teaches homeless children nautical flag signaling. Changes lives.
column67: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: Thank you, Andy.
column68: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Andy: I'm not doing it for you. I'm doing it for the preservation of nautical flag signaling.
column69: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: Dwight, you will be participating.
column70: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Dwight: No thank you.
column71: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: Participation is mandatory; Dwight, but you can choose whatever cause you like.
column72: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Dwight: Fine, I chose the Global Relief Foundation.
column73: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: Great, thank you.
column74: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Dwight: Which was recently discovered to be a front for the Taliban.
column75: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: [everyone groans] Oh, for goodness' sake, Dwight.
column76: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Dwight: Yeah. The Taliban in Afa-ghanistan.
column77: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Creed: The Taliban is the worst. Great heroine, though.
column78: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: Dwight, I cannot have the Taliban on the roster of Operation Give Back.
column79: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Dwight: Well, it looks like there won't be any Operation Give Back. Ha, ha. The nanny state is over, ladies and gentlemen. You're welcome. [wads up Nellie's charity sheet and tosses it toward her]
column80: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: [approaches Roy back at the wedding] There he is. Is it almost time to cut the pancake, or what?
column81: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Roy: Aw, yeah, god, we appreciate everyone coming so early. It's, everyone's just been so nice.
column82: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: Thanks for inviting us, by the way-
column83: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Roy: Are you kidding?
column84: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: That was, that was a surprise.
column85: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Roy: Come on. If it wasn't for you, I never would've met Laura. I mean, seriously, kinda dodged a bullet on that one. [sees Jim's reaction] Just kidding.
column86: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: You're welcome.
column87: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Roy: Thanks...aw.
column88: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: By the way, man, this place is... beautiful.
column89: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Roy: Started a gravel company. I mean, who knew it'd take off?
column90: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: Gravel company?
column91: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Roy: Yeah. What about you? What are you doing?
column92: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: Not gravel, obviously. [both chuckle] No, things are good. Things are good. Got some stuff in the works. So-
column93: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Roy: Oh, cool.
column94: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: Yeah, you never know.
column95: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Kenny: Hey bro, stop wasting time with this haircut. [referring to Jim] He's got a fifty-thousand dollar sports car. Cheers.
column96: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: OK, Kenny.
column97: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Clark: [talking on phone] Duncan, listen, I would love to help you out but where am I gonna find somebody that's pretty, smart and well-informed? Huh? Hold on, hold on. [covers phone's receiver] Erin, do you know anybody that might want... [has realization] Oh my gosh. You love the news, right?
column98: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Erin: Well, it depends. I mean, sometimes I find out things that are really sad.
column99: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Clark: Well, I got a buddy that's a big time local news producer and I can't tell you his name, but it'd blow your mind.
column100: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pete: Uh, is it Duncan?
column101: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Clark: He's looking for on-air talent and he'd kill me if I didn't get you on tape.
column102: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Erin: You mean, put me on the news?
column103: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Clark: You'll just come over, put on little lipstick, loosen up with a glass of red wine and then we'll just run through a few stories. You know, a couple different ways, with a couple different outfits. It'd be really tasteful and it'd really help me out with Duncan... with my friend. [Erin considers] What do you say? Huh?
column104: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Erin: Maybe, ok? Let me think about it.
column105: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Clark: [Pete looks on disappointed] Ok.
column106: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Erin: Whoo!
column107: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Clark: Think it over. [punches Pete]
column108: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pete: No, Clark's not my friend. He is the douche that sits next to me at the office. My friends are Scott, Glenn, and Rob. But, you don't know them.
column109: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Erin: I never really thought much about being more than a receptionist. But, why? Because I happened to answer help wanted ad to be a receptionist? I mean, what if the ad had been for a CEO? Or for a brain surgeon?
column110: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Roy: So, ah, it was a year ago today that I met Laura. I thought she was my waitress and, uh, took her three weeks to tell me that she actually owned the place. You are full of surprises. You are my beautiful mystery girl. And, today, I have a surprise for you. [approaches piano]
column111: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: He plays piano?
column112: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: No. Roy? No.
column113: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Roy: You know how I said I was taking boxing lessons? Actually, I was doing this. Um, so, I hope that you like it. [sits in front of piano]
column114: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Darryl: [clapping] You got this, Roy. [Roy begins playing and singing She's Got a Way by Billy Joel, Pam and Jim looked shocked, Phyllis and Bob begin making out]
column115: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: [in the car] We still surprise each other.
column116: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: Definitely.
column117: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: You know, I never did it, but for your 30th birthday I really wanted to surprise you with-
column118: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: Courtside seats. Sixers.
column119: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: Yes. But, what I didn't tell you is that I actually bought the tickets. We only didn't go because it was-
column120: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: It was an away game.
column121: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: In Phoenix. They should really tell you that more specifically. I mean, every game is an away game for one of the teams. [long pause] Do we know everything about each other?
column122: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: No.
column123: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: Tell me one thing about you I don't know.
column124: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: [laughs] Um, ok. [thinks but says nothing]
column125: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: [in the kitchen] Oh, here's one. Did I ever tell you about the time that my brothers videotaped the lottery announcement? And bought the winning numbers the next day? And then, played the tape for me the next week, and I-
column126: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: And you thought you guys were millionaires.
column127: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: You heard that one.
column128: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: Yes. But there's, wait, oh, there's a funny ending to that story. I can't remember.
column129: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: That I thought we were millionaires.
column130: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Pam: Thought you were millionaires, yeah. That's funny. Shoot, I knew that one.
column131: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: That's all right.
column132: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Angela: The senator and I still have mystery. I'm always waiting to see what he's gonna surprise me with next. [Oscar chokes on his coffee]
column133: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Jim: You all right? [Oscar nods]
column134: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: You support the Taliban abroad. So I assume you're willing to live by their rules here.
column135: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Dwight: Anything else would be inconsistent.
column136: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: Will you join me then in a pledge to live by Taliban law in this office? [offers Dwight a contract]
column137: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Dwight: [takes contract] Absolutely, I will.
column138: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Dwight: I feared Nellie had some sort of a plan but she used a ridiculous font. Huh. [in a fake English accent] You don't have a plan.
column139: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;
column140: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;
column141: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;
column142: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: When you use a ridiculous font, no one thinks you have a plan.

column144: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Dwight: What the? [follows Nellie into the break room]
column145: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: Oh, this is a lovely pen. Ah. But, it's mine now because I stole it.
column146: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Dwight: [taking pen back] Gimme that.
column147: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: Didn't you sign a contract to live under Taliban law? And now, there's been theft. That means, you're not serious or... someone's getting their hand cut off.
column148: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Dwight: You're insane.
column149: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: I know. So, it's better that you pick another charity.
column150: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Dwight: Oh, and let your precious Operation Power Grab proceed unchecked? No thank you.
column151: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: In that case, you... [pulls out a cleaver] will have to chop off my hand.

column153: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Nellie: I tell you what. I need to make three calls. And then after that, you can become a person who chops off people's hands.
column154: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Dwight: Sounds like a plan.

column156: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Erin: Yeah.
column157: 09x02 - Roy's Wedding;Andy: [entering annex] Clark, you and I need to have a little chat. What clothes does Erin need for this news audition?

column358: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Angela: Are you allowed to have pets?
column359: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Oscar: Oh, Angela.
column360: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Dwight: Yesterday I was just your average, ordinary paper salesman with a farm and a bunch of pipe dreams about beet fuel. Today, I leave here a regional manager with a black belt. It really is amazing how your life can change in one day.

column363: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Darryl: We got an offer on the table.
column364: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Jim: What kind of offer?
column365: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Darryl: A buyout.
column366: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Jim: What?
column367: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Darryl: We're in play, baby.
column368: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Jim: Oh, my god!
column369: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Darryl: We did it! Hey, and look, the buyers wanna make sure it's not just a Philly play, so get this: they're gonna pay for us to go pitch out west. We talking Spurs, the Jazz, Cowboys. Blake Griffin, baby.
column370: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Jim: Wow, that is... wow.
column371: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Darryl: Yeah, we did it.
column372: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Jim: Yeah, we did. Hey, how long—how long do we think that's gonna take?
column373: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Darryl: Wade said we could do the whole country in three months.
column374: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Jim: Oh, man. Yeah, I can't do it.
column375: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Darryl: Can't do what?
column376: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Jim: This, man. I can't do this to Pam.
column377: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Darryl: No, no, Jim. This is different. This is everything.
column378: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Jim: I know. And I can't do it.
column379: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Angela: So is your place all bachelor-slobby and gross?
column380: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Oscar: No, it's neat and tasteful, like most gay men's homes. The stereotype holds up.
column381: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Angela: I wouldn't know. I never lived with a gay guy.
column382: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Oscar: Angela, you just were—
column383: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Angela: [starts sobbing] I love him.
column384: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Oscar: I know. I understand more than most, but we both have to move on. You—you can't—
column385: 09x21 - Livin' the Dream;Angela: No, not the senator. I love Dwight.

column49: 09x22/23 - A.A.R.M;Dwight: Have a seat, Phyllis. There we go. As you know, I like to begin each day with an inspirational quote. "Some say the only failure there is is the failure to try." [buzzer sound] That is wrong. Failure of any kind is failure. Jim, over to you.

column199: 09x22/23 - A.A.R.M;Darryl: Wow. Man. I hope he doesn't regret it.

column204: 09x22/23 - A.A.R.M;Jim: An assistant brings their boss coffee with speed and dexterity. But an assistant to the assistant has a thousand times more to prove, am I right?

column229: 09x22/23 - A.A.R.M;Jim: What I'm about to say makes no logical sense, and yet, it might be the most logical thing I've ever said.
column230: 09x22/23 - A.A.R.M;Dwight: Jim, this is gonna come as no surprise but I know exactly what you are going to say. The only possible assistant to my assistant-

column232: 09x22/23 - A.A.R.M;Dwight: Me.
column233: 09x22/23 - A.A.R.M;Jim: The new assistant to the assistant to the regional manager is Dwight K. Schrute.
column234: 09x22/23 - A.A.R.M;Dwight: Yes! [weak applause] Thank you.
column235: 09x22/23 - A.A.R.M;Jim: I think you might want to kneel for this. And yet, the manager for Dunder Mifflin kneels for no one. [Dwight awkwardly squats] That's it. You look really, really good.

column479: 09x24/25 - Finale;Pam: I didn't watch the whole documentary. After a few episodes, it was too painful. I kept wanting to scream at Pam. It took me so long to do so many important things. It's just hard to accept that I spent so many years being less happy than I could have been. Jim was 5 feet from my desk and it took me four years to get to him. It'd be great if people saw this documentary and learned from my mistakes. Not that I'm a tragic person. I'm really happy now. But...it would just...just make my heart soar if someone out there saw this and she said to herself "be strong, trust yourself, love yourself. Conquer your fears. Just go after what you want and act fast, because life just isn't that long."

column507: 09x24/25 - Finale;Oscar: You take something ordinary, like a piece of paper. It's not much. But if you see it in the right way...And that's what you did with this documentary. But seriously, you made a nine-year documentary and you couldn't once show me doing my origami.

column526: 09x24/25 - Finale;Meredith: I just feel lucky that I got a chance to share my crummy story with anyone out there who thinks they're the only one to take a dump in a paper shredder. You're not alone sister. Let's get a beer sometime.
column527: 09x24/25 - Finale;Phyllis: I'm happy that this was all filmed so I can remember everyone and what we did. I worked for a paper company all these years and I never wrote anything down.
column528: 09x24/25 - Finale;Jim: I sold paper at this company for 12 years. My job was to speak to clients on the phone about quantities and types of copier paper. Even if I didn't love every minute of it, everything I have, I owe to this job. This stupid...wonderful...boring...amazing job.
column529: 09x24/25 - Finale;Pam: I thought it was weird when you picked us to make a documentary. But all in all...I think an ordinary paper company like Dunder Mifflin was a great subject for a documentary. There's a lot of beauty in ordinary things. Isn't that kind of the point?
